title: The Tomb of Qin Shi Huang - The Emperor They Buried With an Army

target.note: short declaratives, one idea per beat. Little to no pause between sentences.

narration:
Beneath this field, eight thousand soldiers stand waiting.
They are clay, and they are perfect.
They stand one way for two thousand years.
Their paint left them centuries after burial.
They are called the Terracotta Army.
Eight thousand soldiers in the dark.
Six hundred horses stood beside them.
They stand in long rows, in earthen pits.
They are all guarding one man.
His name is Qin Shi Huang.
He was the first emperor of all China.
In 221 BC he ended centuries of war.
China had been a hundred separate kingdoms.
He gave them one script and one ruler.
One set of weights for every trade.
That one ruler was himself.
He burned every book that disagreed with him.
The scholars who hid them went down too.
Work started on it in 246 BC.
It took decades of forced labor, unpaid.
The mound above the grave copied a pyramid.
They called the whole burial a heavenly palace.
The whole complex lies outside Xi'an.
Every single soldier is a different height.
No two of the faces are the same.
Then the army vanished for two thousand years.
In 1974 farmers were digging a well.
A shovel struck something hard in the dirt.
It was a clay shoulder, then a face.
The clay broke when the diggers raised it.
So the hole was covered over and abandoned.
In 2012 a new pit was opened.
More than a thousand soldiers lay inside.
Two bronze cranes lay broken in the dirt.
Archaeologists repaired them with modern glue anyway.
In 1983 a scientist poured acid on figures.
Nobody can read those markings ever again.
Soil samples from the mound gave up mercury.
Enough of it to fill a small pool.
The old records say rivers of liquid mercury.
Mercury is a slow poison.
The body never really lets it go.
The main chamber has never been opened once.
It lies under the mound, still sealed.
Behind the army, the door stays shut.

beats.line: Beneath this field, eight thousand soldiers stand waiting.
beats.visual: wide empty flat brown dirt field outside Xi'an, low horizon, nothing on screen; hand-lettered label 'OUTSIDE XI'AN, CHINA'

beats.line: They are clay, and they are perfect.
beats.visual: cut into the soil: a clay soldier standing upright, undisturbed, dust on its shoulders

beats.line: They stand one way for two thousand years.
beats.visual: the same clay figure held, full frame, cropped at both side edges

beats.line: Their paint left them centuries after burial.
beats.visual: close on the figure's shoulder and face, paint flaking away in flakes on the dirt

beats.line: They are called the Terracotta Army.
beats.visual: hand-lettered 'TERRACOTTA ARMY' stamped across the top of a rank of clay figures

beats.line: Eight thousand soldiers in the dark.
beats.visual: a dark earthen pit in cross-section, rows of clay figures standing shoulder to shoulder below ground

beats.line: Six hundred horses stood beside them.
beats.visual: two clay horses, harnessed, filling the frame, cropped at the left edge

beats.line: They stand in long rows, in earthen pits.
beats.visual: long ranks of warriors receding into the dark of the pit, the rows continuing past the frame

beats.line: They are all guarding one man.
beats.visual: all the clay faces turned the same direction; the character standing among them, small

beats.line: His name is Qin Shi Huang.
beats.visual: name stamp 'QIN SHI HUANG'; character below it, pointing up at the stamp

beats.line: He was the first emperor of all China.
beats.visual: character full body before a plain map of China; speech bubble 'first emperor'

beats.line: In 221 BC he ended centuries of war.
beats.visual: calendar page marked '221 BC'; crossed arrows and broken banners on the map

beats.line: China had been a hundred separate kingdoms.
beats.visual: map covered in many small red kingdom shapes with fighting arrows between them

beats.line: He gave them one script and one ruler.
beats.visual: the red shapes merging into one outline; one road, one script sheet, one crown

beats.line: One set of weights for every trade.
beats.visual: a set of bronze weights of different shapes, all stamped with one mark

beats.line: That one ruler was himself.
beats.visual: a single figure on a throne, arms folded; character below, deadpan; speech bubble 'himself'

beats.line: He burned every book that disagreed with him.
beats.visual: a stack of old books going into a fire, hand-drawn flames

beats.line: The scholars who hid them went down too.
beats.visual: a robed scholar figure lowered into a pit; character recoiling from the edge

beats.line: Work started on it in 246 BC.
beats.visual: plan of the tomb complex drawn on a wall; one square block marked '246 BC'

beats.line: It took decades of forced labor, unpaid.
beats.visual: long lines of laborers hauling earth, drawn small and repeating to the horizon

beats.line: The mound above the grave copied a pyramid.
beats.visual: the earth mound drawn beside a small stepped pyramid silhouette; label 'pyramid'

beats.line: They called the whole burial a heavenly palace.
beats.visual: the mound sketched as a celestial palace: stars, a moon disc, cloud bands

beats.line: The whole complex lies outside Xi'an.
beats.visual: a simple hand-drawn map plan with a dot east of a walled city; label 'OUTSIDE XI'AN'

beats.line: Every single soldier is a different height.
beats.visual: three clay soldiers side by side, heights visibly different; a measuring stick behind them

beats.line: No two of the faces are the same.
beats.visual: two clay faces side by side, clearly different; label 'no two the same'

beats.line: Then the army vanished for two thousand years.
beats.visual: the empty field again, quiet; character small at the edge of frame

beats.line: In 1974 farmers were digging a well.
beats.visual: 1974; two farmers swinging pickaxes beside a half-dug well

beats.line: A shovel struck something hard in the dirt.
beats.visual: shovel blade striking something hard, clay chipping off the edge

beats.line: It was a clay shoulder, then a face.
beats.visual: a clay shoulder and a clay face emerging from the dirt, loose soil falling

beats.line: The clay broke when the diggers raised it.
beats.visual: hands lifting a broken clay arm, fragments dropping back into the pit

beats.line: So the hole was covered over and abandoned.
beats.visual: the pit filled in, covered with a tarp and a small building over it

beats.line: In 2012 a new pit was opened.
beats.visual: plan view of an L-shaped corridor of vaults; label 'PIT 1, 2012'

beats.line: More than a thousand soldiers lay inside.
beats.visual: the L-shaped pit filled with clay figures, seen from above, cropped at both edges

beats.line: Two bronze cranes lay broken in the dirt.
beats.visual: two bronze crane figures lying in fragments on the dirt, both broken

beats.line: Archaeologists repaired them with modern glue anyway.
beats.visual: a modern glue brush and epoxy bottle drawn next to a repaired crane body

beats.line: In 1983 a scientist poured acid on figures.
beats.visual: a figure pouring acid from a jar onto terracotta armor; surface dissolving

beats.line: Nobody can read those markings ever again.
beats.visual: the same armor plate greyed out, its painted surface gone; character looking away

beats.line: Soil samples from the mound gave up mercury.
beats.visual: a soil sample jar in a lab tray; a bright silver bead forming inside

beats.line: Enough of it to fill a small pool.
beats.visual: a low tunnel with a shallow pool of liquid mercury reflecting the lamp

beats.line: The old records say rivers of liquid mercury.
beats.visual: an old scroll unrolling; painted on it: two winding silver rivers around a shape

beats.line: Mercury is a slow poison.
beats.visual: a silver droplet on a fingertip; character wiping his mouth; label 'poison'

beats.line: The body never really lets it go.
beats.visual: a body outline with the silver still lodged in it, drawn flat

beats.line: The main chamber has never been opened once.
beats.visual: a heavy stone door in the dark, shut; one flat painted guard figure beside it

beats.line: It lies under the mound, still sealed.
beats.visual: the sealed mound in cross-section: outer pits, then solid earth, then a black sealed void

beats.line: Behind the army, the door stays shut.
beats.visual: the shut stone door again, held; character very small in the dark beside it; speech bubble 'nobody has opened it'
